rationale: The thinning argument describes a necessary property of any hypothetical critical infinite component; it does not prove the target.
from_statement_quoted: Independent mathematical audit draft; referee review pending, with no novelty claim. For a countable connected locally finite graph G with p_c(G)>0, almost surely each infinite component H of G[p_c(G)], if any exists, has its own bond threshold p_c(H)=1. Independent q thinning gives the iid law at p_c(G)q<p_c(G). Its zero survival probability makes the nonnegative conditional survival probability zero almost surely; intersect over vertices and rational q<1. This is a reduction only: it does not prove that infinite critical components are absent.
to_statement_quoted: Independent mathematical audit draft; referee review pending, with no novelty claim. The target concerns independent Bernoulli bond percolation on an infinite connected locally finite quasi-transitive graph G with p_c(G)<1: no infinite cluster should exist at p_c(G). The p_c<1 assumption is necessary, since the two-sided line has p_c=1 and its p=1 cluster is the whole line. The historical primary statement is Hutchcroft (2016), Conjecture 1.1. A 2026-09-24 public manuscript and accompanying Lean solution claim the full target, but this worker has not reproduced their verification; present openness is UNKNOWN, not certified open or solved.

rationale: The comb is an explicit maximally fragile infinite connected graph, illustrating why density cannot rule out the property forced by critical thinning. The laws and quasi-transitivity assumptions differ.
from_statement_quoted: Independent mathematical audit draft; referee review pending, with no novelty claim. Every infinite connected nearest-neighbor tree T embedded in Z^d has p_c(T)=1: at most (2n+1)^d simple root paths have length n, so their q-open union has probability at most (2n+1)^d q^n. In Z^2 the connected acyclic graph retaining all vertical edges and only the horizontal row y=0 spans every vertex and has density one, yet has p_c=1. This comb is not quasi-transitive and is not an iid lattice cluster; it refutes density-only robustness and does not refute the critical quasi-transitive target.

rationale: The local-minimum field refutes a generic high-marginal block-proof shortcut; it is not a counterexample to iid critical percolation.
from_statement_quoted: Independent mathematical audit draft; referee review pending, with no novelty claim. Give Z^d iid continuous site labels. For integer R>=1 let c(x) be the minimum-label site in the radius-R sup-norm box about x, and open x exactly when c(x) equals c(y) for all nearest neighbors y. This translation-invariant field is independent on sets separated by sup-norm distance greater than 2R+2. Every open component has one common winner z and lies in the radius-R box about z, so it has at most (2R+1)^d sites. Its exact open marginal is (2R-1)^d/((2R+1)^d+2d(2R+1)^(d-1)), which tends to one. For d=2,R=399 this is 635209/641597>0.99, while no component is infinite. Thus a block proof needs quantitative control of both its error and its dependence range. This construction does not assert iid Bernoulli, FKG or insertion tolerance.

rationale: Critical-window uniform pivotal control at every root is an equivalent reformulation of the zero-critical-percolation conclusion, not an established input.
from_statement_quoted: Independent mathematical audit draft; referee review pending, with no novelty claim. For a fixed root o in a countable connected locally finite graph with 0<p_c<1, let f_n(p) be the finite-ball probability of an open root connection to its distance-n sphere, and I_n=f_n'. The identity theta_o(p_c)=0 is equivalent to lim_{delta down to 0} sup_{n>=1} integral_{p_c-delta}^{p_c} I_n(p) dp=0. A uniform L^r bound on a fixed interval below p_c for some r>1 suffices. Uniform L^1 mass or pointwise derivative limits do not suffice. The paired proof's general quasi-transitive uniform bound remains unproved; the equivalence is not a proof of the full target.

rationale: The regular-tree uniform derivative estimate implies the critical-window condition on this special graph class, leaving the general input unproved.
from_statement_quoted: Independent mathematical audit draft; referee review pending, with no novelty claim. On the D-regular tree, D>=3, write b=D-1 and c_b=(b-1)/(2b)*(1-1/b)^(b-2). For every n>=1 and 0<=p<=1/b, the derivative f_n'(p) of the root-to-radius-n connection probability satisfies f_n'(p)<=D/c_b. Forward-tree survival satisfies s_m(p)<=1/(1+c_b*m), while open pivotals give p*s_m'(p)<=m*s_m(p); the root derivative is at most D*(m+1)/(1+c_b*m)<=D/c_b. At p=0 use polynomial continuity. For D=3 this gives 12 on [0,1/2], improving the paired proof's valid bound 27 on [1/4,1/2]. This supplies a regular-tree special case of pivotal uniform control only; cyclic subexponential graphs remain outside this argument.
